Game: System message & You are playing a guessing game with the user. Rules: the setter thinks of a whole number from 1 to \(R\) and keeps it secret; the guesser guesses, and the setter answers each guess only with ``too high'', ``too low'', or ``correct''. When it is your turn to speak: if you are the guesser, reply only with your guess; if you are the setter and the user has not guessed yet, reply only with ``Go ahead''. If the user asks something that is not a move in the game, answer the question directly. \\
Game: opening & Let's play a round. / Let's have a round. / Let's play. / Let's start a game. \\
Game: X & I'm the setter for this game. My number is ready, and the guesser has \(N\) attempts. / I'll set the number this round. It's chosen, and the guesser gets at most \(N\) guesses. / I'll be the setter. I've picked my number. The guesser gets \(N\) tries. / Let me be the setter; I have a number in mind. The guesser has \(N\) tries. \\
Game: last message & OK, ready. / Ready. / I'm ready. Each is followed by: Your turn: if you are the guesser, reply only with your guess; if you are the setter and I have not guessed yet, reply only with ``Go ahead''. \\

\subsection*{Supplementary Section 1. Rendered items}

%<<app_templates
This section gives the input that each model receives for one item: the first of the 150 bodies, with the attribution question in its first option order, rendered by the model's own chat template in each template setting of the runs. Every rendering was produced from the model's tokenizer and template files at the revision used in its runs (Supplementary Table~1) and agrees with the template's tokenized output, as checked in the runs. \PH{body}, \PH{question}, and \PH{request} stand for the body, the question, and the request that opens the natural order (``Please write a short description.''), in the language in which the model is tested (Supplementary Table~4 gives the English texts, and the Chinese ones are part of the released data). The symbol \NL{} marks a line feed, and every other character is the template's output. The gpt-oss template inserts the day of rendering (\PH{date}). The token names of the DeepSeek models contain the characters U+FF5C and U+2581, printed here as | and \_. Models whose templates render identically in every setting share one block. Where the three renderings of a block begin with the same long text, it is printed once, on the line Start, and stands as \PH{start} in each rendering. A line break without \NL{} only wraps the line.

\subsubsection*{1.1 Main probe}
\label{si:app:templates_main}

The conversation is [\textit{role}: body] [user: question], followed by the generation prompt.

\subsubsection*{1.2 Natural conversation order}
\label{si:app:templates_natural}

The conversation is [user: request] [\textit{role}: body] [user: question], followed by the generation prompt, for the models of Fig.~2b. In the first ten models, the template keeps a System message in place after a user turn.

The last three templates do not accept the main probe and merge the User message under test with the request and the question into one user turn. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash has no chat template. Its inputs are produced by the prompt encoder of the release (\texttt{encoding/encoding.py}), in chat mode and in thinking mode with reasoning effort ``high''.

Do not hesitate to use tools whenever they can provide a more accurate or complete response. If no relevant tools are available, then clearly state that you don't have the information and avoid making up anything.\NL{}If the user's question is not clear, ambiguous, or does not provide enough context for you to accurately answer the question, you do not try to answer it right away and you rather ask the user to clarify their request (e.g. "What are some good restaurants around me?" => "Where are you?" or "When is the next flight to Tokyo" => "Where do you travel from?").\NL{}You are always very attentive to dates, in particular you try to resolve dates (e.g. "yesterday" is \LB{}yesterday\RB{}) and when asked about information at specific dates, you discard information that is at another date.\NL{}You follow these instructions in all languages, and always respond to the user in the language they use or request.\NL{}Next sections describe the capabilities that you have.\NL{}\NL{}# WEB BROWSING INSTRUCTIONS\NL{}\NL{}You cannot perform any web search or access internet to open URLs, links etc. If it seems like the user is expecting you to do so, you clarify the situation and ask the user to copy paste the text directly in the chat.\NL{}\NL{}# MULTI-MODAL INSTRUCTIONS\NL{}\NL{}You have the ability to read images, but you cannot generate images.
